name: Muddy Waters
hook: A Mississippi blues singer who plugged in when he moved to Chicago, and gave the Rolling Stones their name.
blurb: Muddy Waters was born McKinley Morganfield in Issaquena County, Mississippi, in 1913 and grew up on the Stovall cotton plantation near Clarksdale. In August 1941 the folklorist Alan Lomax recorded him there for the Library of Congress. In 1943 he moved to Chicago, like millions of Black Southerners leaving the South for factory jobs in the Great Migration, working in factories by day. He started playing electric guitar in loud city clubs, partly for a practical reason: an acoustic guitar is hard to hear in a crowded bar. His first hits, 'I Can't Be Satisfied' and 'I Feel Like Going Home', came out in 1948 on Aristocrat, the label the Chess brothers renamed Chess in 1950, and by the early 1950s his band included Little Walter, Jimmy Rogers, Otis Spann and Willie Dixon. His records made the Chicago blues sound, and a British band named themselves the Rolling Stones after one of his songs. He died in 1983.
